19 September 2011 
 
• 
Gold saw frantic ranges last week, touching $1765 
basis December gold at one point before rallying 
back to former levels of congestion around $1825. 
Given the extra-ordinary attention paid to Greece, 
and the possible consequence not only for other 
‘southern’ Eurozone member states of a Greek de-
fault, but for the very integrity of the European pro-
ject, gold has been restrained, and that  implies that 
wise longs have been happy to let get go of their 
longs into a willing marketplace. Silver and the 
PGMs suffered partly through gold’s fall, and partly 
through a sequence of poor economic data. We see  
money being pulled out of the precious space and 
tend to assume it is a natural response to margin 
pressure, but it is worth nothing that money is flow-
ing out of equities rapidly.  
 
 
• 
Overall, we are seeing declines in investor position-
ing under the pressure of volatility and price de-
clines., as investor sentiment struggles against the 
headwinds of Europe, poor US growth, and some 
concerns over China—rising inflation and slowing 
growth there combined with regional debt burdens? 
 
• 
Gold and Silver saw ETF inflows as the macro pic-
ture still remains gold supportive in a time of nega-
tive real interest rates and heightened risk, with sil-
ver largely along for the ride. The PGMS are none 
the less underperforming in response to rational 
economic concerns—the same ones that may serve 
to underpin gold.

19 September 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
Gold made the high of the week on Monday with 
the daily high of $1865.20 basis December fu-
tures, and slumped off to $1804 on a high-volume 
day, in a week that would see a range of 
US$99.80, making the low on Friday the 16th. It 
was difficult to see what the driver was when so 
many of the factors governing gold’s recent rally 
remained in place, however, which so many rea-
sons ‘to buy’ it also made sense for healthy longs 
to take profit whilst those factors remained in 
place—particularly as ‘headline risk’ of Eurozone 
leaders launching an all out assault to save 
Greece, and by extension the Euro, was high. 
The market essentially traded ‘risk off’ before  
looking over-sold and finishing the week with 
what looks like a corrective move back to $1825 
Decembers. The week ended with a return of 
Japanese and HK physical buying. 
 
• 
Last week saw a decent reduction in the net long 
speculative positions by 1.80 million Troy ounces 
as the rapid plunge forced margined positions 
out. TOCOM quietly accumulated just over 220 k 
gold to take the non-commercial longs to almost 
1.30 million tozs long. 
 
• 
ETF investors added around one lakh of gold to 
their positions, taking us to almost 68 million tozs 
gof gold held by that sector.

19 September 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Silver ETF Investment, Jan 07—September 11 
• 
The silver price volatility of the previous week 
ending the 9th saw silver resolving sharply down-
wards to ‘almost’ test big technical supports in the 
price, finding support at $39.40 Dec, testing that 
again, and then moving smartly higher for the 
close of the week. The picture is rather mixed 
with a key area of support around $39.12, and not 
helped by price action in Copper. Technically, the 
long term uptrend looks intact basis Ichimoku 
clouds, but note that this week saw the break of 
the uptrend in our figure charts—the last time this 
happened was July, and the uptrend was re-
sumed rather quickly so we will keep an eye on 
this. 
 
 
• 
Silver a decline of almost 11 million tozs spec 
positioning to September 13th. It will be interest-
ing to see how these figures compare with the 
next release, basis subsequent price moves. Re-
cent volatility and selling in other markets will 
have places longs under a fair amount of pres-
sure regarding margins, especially as some in-
vestors may have struggled with crude markets. 
 
 
• 
ETFs saw continued buying interest, taking hold-
ings up to 458.670 Million tozs, an increase of 
3.845 million on the week.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
19 September 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
Platinum dropped to levels not seen since early 
August last week as Euro zone disruption displaced 
concerns over supply, and cost pressures. $1770 
seems to be the area where buying interest turns 
the selling around, although $1755-1760 seems 
even more secure as a support level in the short 
term. With a week when core retail sales, unem-
ployment, the Empire State manufacturing index 
and the Philly Fed all came in looking gloomy in-
deed, and there was fresh movement to break the 
deadlock on US home foreclosure, and it was not 
surprising that Platinum was struggling. 
 
• 
Net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX 
ounces dropped by almost 90,000 Tozs.  Is it again 
a question of trading around the Profit taking on the 
Platinum-gold spread, or symptomatic of wider risk 
reduction? 
 
 
• 
Platinum ETF holdings decreased very slightly over 
the week. ETF holdings are nonetheless very close 
to their all-time highs however.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
19 September 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—September 11 
Palladium ETF Investment, Apr 07—September 11 
• 
Palladium skidded to a low right from the start of the 
week. A natural bounce to $737 resistance took 
place but we ended the week with a rather weak 
tone, unable to break back higher and the trend be-
ing ‘down’ - helped along by a series of poor eco-
nomic numbers as well. We held the important 
$700-705 level— it is important now, but won’t be if 
we close below it on the daily. So far it has held (in 
that we have closed above it) five times so far. 
 
 
• 
Net long speculative positions in palladium on NY-
MEX saw a decline of just over a quarter a million 
tozs in the week to September 13th. Patient  longs 
must be under significant pressure, considering the 
recent batterings they have had since the beginning 
of August. 
 
• 
Net palladium Exchange Traded Fund flows were  a 
small negative, taking the overall positions to just 
over 2 million tozs now.
